title: Compact Remediator Store + Live Scripter for One-Click Fixes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Short: Build a lightweight 'remediator' registry and a Live Scripter UI/CLI to surface vetted one‑click fixes for common operator actions. Goals: reduce time-to-remediate for oncall, ensure safe idempotent fixes, make runbooks executable as atomic artifacts.

Background: Oncall repeatedly runs small ad-hoc scripts to restore capacity, recycle pods, clear caches, or reconfigure routing. We want a curated store (YAML manifest) of small remediator artifacts with metadata (inputs, required RBAC, side-effects, telemetry hooks, rollback steps). The Live Scripter will let an operator preview the plan, run dry-run, and then execute with a single confirmation. The remediator store will be integrated into the runbooks-as-tasks registry and the Console quickfix surface.

Scope: prototype remediator registry service, CLI for authoring/publishing a remediator, Live Scripter UI component in Console Quickfix modal, execution sandbox (k8s Job wrapper + timeouts + circuit breaker), telemetry for executed remediations, audit logs, and RBAC checks.

Out of scope: full policy engine (handled by separate RBAC project), scheduling/autonomous decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Registry service stores remediator manifests and serves list/describe endpoints
CLI can publish a remediator with schema validation and lint warnings
Console Live Scripter shows remediator details, renders inputs, allows dry-run and execute
Execution path enforces RBAC, logs audit event, emits telemetry metric remediator.exec.count
All remediators require a rollback section or explicit confirmation acknowledging irreversible actions
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after oncall debrief. Noted recurring cache purge pattern (PG-Cache-12) that took ~9m to remediate manually.
2025-02-21 - Marco Ruiz: Spike completed. Prototype registry implemented (Go HTTP + sqlite) and basic CLI. Found race when two publishes happen simultaneously — added optimistic locking.
2025-02-25 - Priya Menon (SRE): Reviewed prototype. Concern: remediator side-effects need stricter gating for multi-tenant clusters. Asked for extra RBAC checks and KMS audit.
2025-03-01 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented dry-run mode and k8s Job sandbox with 2m timeout and pod security policy. Added telemetry hooks to emit remediator.exec.start/end events.
2025-03-04 - Design (Evan Cho): Quickfix modal mockups uploaded. Suggested inline diff of resources changed, and explicit rollback button placement.

2025-03-05 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Security review requested. Marked high risk for remediators that modify routing table. Action: compile list of high-risk patterns and require a secondary approver.
next_steps: Finish schema for remediator manifest and publish to Confluence
Add server-side publish validation for 'safety_profile' and required rollback
Wire Console Quickfix modal to registry list endpoint and import design mocks
Add end-to-end test simulating remediator dry-run and execute in ephemeral cluster
Prepare PR for security review including threat model and KMS integration notes
implementation_notes: Use existing admin-runbook-service model for list/describe endpoints but keep separate DB namespace to limit blast radius
Registry will accept a small templating language (Go templates) for inputs; avoid full JS evaluation to reduce risk
Execution layer uses k8s Jobs in a dedicated namespace with resource quotas and network egress deny-by-default
Telemetry: increment remediator.exec.count, remediator.exec.duration_ms, remediator.exec.result with tags (remediator_id, team, outcome)
risks_mitigations: Risk: accidental destructive remediators executed in prod — Mitigation: require explicit 'irreversible' flag, secondary approver and 2FA for such remediators
Risk: leaking secrets in remediator logs — Mitigation: automatic redact of KMS-referenced secrets and advise use of sealed secrets
Risk: schema drift between CLI and Console — Mitigation: CI validation and versioned manifests
